about: Published numbers for the day and night plan (services/regime.py). The child's own logs come first; these numbers fill gaps and give the wide range that is common for the age. Minutes, except counts and shares. Clock times are minutes after midnight. low/high are the limits that the source gives (see range).

notes.text: A young baby has no fixed day and night rhythm yet. The rhythm starts at about 8 to 9 weeks and gets clearer at about 15 weeks. The times in this plan are a guide, not a target.
Newborns feed 8 to 12 times in 24 hours, also at night. In the first weeks, do not let more than about 4 hours pass at night without a feed. Wake the baby if necessary.
At 5 weeks about 1 baby in 10 sleeps 5 hours or more in one stretch. At 3 months it is about 1 in 2.
The longest sleep at night gets longer in these months: from about 5 hours to about 7 hours on average. The spread between babies is large.

Night feeds are still common. Many formula-fed babies do not need a feed in the middle of the night from 2 to 4 months, or when they weigh more than 5.4 kg. Breastfed babies usually feed at night for longer.
Most babies of this age still wake at night: about 8 in 10 wake 1 time or more, and about 6 in 10 still have a milk feed at night. Breastfed and formula-fed babies are the same in this.
A baby who does not sleep 6 or 8 hours in one stretch at 6 or 12 months does not develop less well.
The morning wake time stays almost the same as a baby gets older. An earlier bedtime gives a longer night.
Most children change from 2 naps to 1 nap between about 15 and 24 months. The change is not a clean step: days with 1 nap and days with 2 naps mix for some weeks.
Almost all children of this age still nap: fewer than 3 in 100 stop before 2 years.
Night sleep stays almost the same from 1 to 5 years. The total gets lower because day sleep gets shorter.
About 9 in 10 children nap at 2 years, and about 5 in 10 at 3 years. Age is a weak sign of the last nap. Your child's own days decide.
A nap late in the day can move the time that a child falls asleep at night. In one study, children of about 3 years who napped fell asleep about 1 hour later at night.
About half of the children of this age still nap. Many nap on some days only. Between studies, the share that has stopped at 3 years goes from 5 in 100 to 65 in 100.
Night sleep stays almost the same from 1 to 5 years. When the nap stops, the night does not get much longer.
Regular times help: bedtime and wake time within about 30 minutes each day. The authors of this guideline say that the evidence for the number is weak.
Most children of this age do not nap: about 8 in 10 have stopped by 4 to 5 years. Some still nap on some days.
Regular times help: bedtime and wake time within about 30 minutes each day. The authors of this guideline say that the evidence for the number is weak.

sleep_bands.about: Hours of sleep in 24 hours, National Sleep Foundation 2015, Table 2. rec = recommended; ok = may be appropriate (the expert panel did not agree); outside ok = not recommended.

nap_limit.about: From about 2 years, when the night sleep suffers: a nap of 2 hours at most, awake by 15:00.
